applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (extended to Gibraltar)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Bermuda Exempted Companies Act 1981 (Part IV, as amended); Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 Part 24 (Overseas Companies); Gibraltar Proceeds of Crime Act 2015; Gibraltar Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2019 (AMLCFT Act); Gibraltar Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2019; GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes 2023.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Bermuda Supreme Court / UK FCDO)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing from Bermuda
UBO and Director KYC forms (including source of wealth declarations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization then Consular Legalization or Hague Apostille, as required by Gibraltar authorities

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for PEPs per GFSC AML/CFT Rules; screening of all UBOs and directors against the Gibraltar/UK HMT OFSI consolidated list, EU consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council listing, and U.S. OFAC SDN list (best practice). Adverse media and FATF high-risk jurisdiction checks are also applied.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry (official e-Registry portal: csra.gi)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script; English is the default corporate language. Names in other scripts are accepted only when Romanized and certified by a professional translator; the legal registered name must be Latin-script.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written appeal to the Registrar of Companies within 21 days of the rejection notice, specifying grounds for reconsideration. The Registrar issues a determination within 15 working days; further referral to the Minister for Financial Services is available. A fresh name application may be submitted at any time without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is accepted for correspondence only; it does not satisfy the statutory registered office requirement. The registered office in Gibraltar must be a physical street address staffed during normal business hours and available for service of process under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 and AMLCFT Act.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% - unannounced physical inspections are conducted by the GFSC and law enforcement on a risk-assessed basis; for a low-risk PropTech SaaS company with no physical premises, the likelihood is low but not zero.

Notarization and consular legalization bundle (if required)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1930 (Gibraltar), as amended; ss. 5–15 (incorporation and memorandum), ss. 27–36 (registered office, directors and secretary), and the Gibraltar Companies (Amendment) Act 2018 for certain reporting provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission, Eurotowers 4, 1 Europort Road, Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form GIC-01 Application for Incorporation together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association and Statement of First Directors and Secretary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued or paid-up capital is required; the company may be formed with one ordinary share of no par or nominal value. No escrow account or blocked deposit is required for the initial share capital, but issued shares must be fully subscribed and paid within the timeframe set in the Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the offer by the subscribers to subscribe for the ordinary shares set opposite their names in the share allotment schedule is accepted, and the allotment and payment terms are approved; (2) the registered office at [registered agent address], Gibraltar, is adopted as the company's statutory registered office for service of process; (3) the persons named in the Statement of First Directors are appointed to hold office as directors; (4) the secretary named in the statutory records is appointed; and (5) the directors are collectively authorized to execute all incorporation completion documents, file the requisite statutory returns, and open corporate banking and payment accounts as needed for the PropTech SaaS business. Passed by unanimous written consent of the first directors pursuant to the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation application and constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form GIC-01 through the Gibraltar Companies House online portal, annexing the signed Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A), the Statement of First Directors and Secretary, and each director's signed consent to act. If the portal requires identity authentication, provide notarized copies of passports and utility bills for all first directors and the ultimate beneficial owner. Pay the prescribed filing fee electronically and retain the submission receipt. After preliminary validation, the registry will issue a tailored query list or proceed to incorporation.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statement of First Directors and Secretary
Consent to Act forms for each director and the secretary
Notarized passport and residence proof for each director and beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the incorporator has 14 days to respond through the same portal with corrected M&A provisions or revised KYC packs; refiling attracts no additional registry fee unless the economic substance questionnaire has been triggered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and company number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Monitor the portal notification for issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. Download the machine-scanned certificate, the company number, the official date of incorporation, and the validated M&A stamped by the registry. Retain the certificate as the indispensable legal evidence of corporate existence for all downstream bank, tax, and licensing actions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated within the service level, contact the Companies House helpdesk with the payment receipt and portal submission reference; a resolution is normally issued via an expedited correction procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt registered office and establish statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent and Companies House Records Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File notice of the adopted Gibraltar registered office with the Registrar and physically maintain the statutory registers at the office of the licensed corporate service provider. The registers must include members, directors, secretary, persons with significant control, and charges. The registered agent must confirm in writing that the address is a physical place in Gibraltar and that service of process can be accepted.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the submitted address is rejected because the premises are not a valid service address, the company must file a revised notice of registered office using a new Gibraltar address and pay the applicable amendment fee within 21 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pass first board resolution, appoint officers, and issue shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors of the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution in accordance with the Articles. Approve the allotment schedule, appoint directors and the corporate secretary, adopt the registered office, confirm the accounting reference date, and authorize opening of bank/EMI accounts. Issue share certificates and enter allotments in the register of members within two months of allotment.
required_dossiers: Register of Members and Allotment Schedule
Register of Directors and Register of Secretaries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum challenge arises, rely on the Articles' written resolution provision to validate the resolution; if the share payment is queried by the registered agent, provide the bank statement evidencing the share subscription payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax and social insurance notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar Income Tax Office and Gibraltar Director of Social Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the company registration form with the Income Tax Office to obtain a Gibraltar tax reference number, and register as an employer if any payroll staff are engaged in Gibraltar. Complete the Company Registration Form, the details of resident or non-resident officers, and the expected principal income sources. For a pure cloud SaaS company, no branch license is required.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution on taxation and accounting period
List of directors with personal tax identification numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Income Tax Office questions the company's factual tax residence or economic activity, prepare the board-approved service contract and substance explanation; late filing penalties may be mitigated by voluntary disclosure within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Accredit corporate governance records for AML and PSC requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission and Beneficial Ownership Secure Search System (BOSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enter the ultimate beneficial owner and persons with significant control into the Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) system through the licensed agent. File the annual confirmation statement once operational and reconcile the ownership data with the platform's cap table. Retain board minutes covering any subsequent allotments or service agreements.
required_dossiers: Register of Persons with Significant Control
Consent of licensed agent for BOSS submission
AML risk assessment for Low_Risk_Standard SaaS payment profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BOSS entry is rejected, correct the beneficial ownership details and resubmit through the same agent; any mismatch between the cap table and statutory PSC register must be cured by board resolution before resubmission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing authority is triggered for ISIC 6201 (computer programming and related software activities) operating as a PropTech SaaS platform.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required by industrial law; the company may optionally maintain an outward-facing PSD2/EMD payment-agent filing only if it facilitates collections beyond Stripe Billing or ACH Direct.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: HM Government of Gibraltar Department of Environment, Heritage and Climate Change
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required / Exempt — pure office/cloud activity with no manufacturing plant, construction works, or licensed discharge point.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, or stack emission thresholds apply. The company must, however, comply with the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations for any server hardware disposed in Gibraltar, and ensure that any future subleased data center capacity meets the environmental noise and energy reporting standards of the landlord.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire-service operational permit is required for a virtual registered office. If employees later occupy physical office premises, the company must obtain a Fire Safety Certificate, complete a workplace risk assessment, and pass the relevant electrical installation condition report and first-aid compliance check before opening the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar – Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax), Ministry of Fiscal Affairs; portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation. Corporate registry: Gibraltar Companies House (Registrar of Companies). Customs/indirect-tax authority: HM Customs & Excise Department, Gibraltar, https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/customs. For Bermuda domestic tax-exempt status: Bermuda Registrar of Companies and the Ministry of Finance (Economic Substance filings), portal: https://www.bermudabusinessregistry.com.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Engage a Gibraltar registered agent, secure a registered office, and file the prescribed Foreign Company Registration application with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 2014 within one month of establishing a place of business, thereby obtaining a Gibraltar Company Number. Step 2: Within 30 days of commencing a tax presence, file the Income Tax Office Company Registration Application (prescribed form, accompanied by the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, constitutional documents, shareholder/director registers and registered office consent) to procure the Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (GTRN), which is the sole statutory corporate tax identifier. Step 3: If payroll exists in the Gibraltar PE, submit the PAYE Employer Registration form to the Income Tax Office and obtain a PAYE deduction reference. Step 4: File the equivalent Bermuda Economic Substance Registration/Declaration with the Bermuda Registrar's BERT platform because the entity is an Exempted Company undertaking relevant activity outside Bermuda; Bermuda issues its own Economic Substance Compliance number but no tax ID since Bermuda levies no income tax. Step 5: No separate VAT/TIN registration is required or available because neither Gibraltar nor Bermuda operates VAT/GST; the GTRN and Bermuda Company Number cover national tax identity purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (the Bermuda Exempted Company is statutorily tax-exempt in Bermuda under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 until 2035 and has no Bermuda taxable income. For Gibraltar source exposure, the entity is a non-resident foreign company subject to Entity_Level_Taxation in respect only of profits attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment, at the corporate rate of 10% on assessable profit up to £10 million and 12.5% above £10 million; profits from foreign clients without a Gibraltar PE fall within Territorial_Scope exclusion. The entity is not Pass_Through_Eligible; it remains a taxable legal person in both Bermuda and Gibraltar).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not provide a US-style check-the-box or fiscal-transparency election. Available elections/treatments: (1) election to be assessed under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010 as a non-resident company relying on the UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Arrangement 1952 where management and control remains outside Gibraltar; (2) historically Qualifying Company status (closed to new entrants since 31 December 2010; grandfathering only, of no value to a new PropTech SaaS); (3) election for economic-substance compliance location: the company may elect to attribute the relevant activity to the Gibraltar PE and file the Bermuda Economic Substance Declaration reflecting substance performed in Gibraltar; (4) hybrid mismatch election: none beneficial — Gibraltar implements the OECD hybrid-mismatch rules, disallowing double-deduction structures, and the Sail-backed Bermuda entity cannot make a transparency election for Gibraltar or UK tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Nil – Gibraltar does not operate a VAT or GST. Gibraltar indirect taxation is limited to customs import duties, excise duties on alcohol/tobacco/fuel, and international services no consumption tax. Bermuda equally imposes no VAT, GST, or general sales tax on goods or SaaS revenues. If SaaS is supplied to UK non-business consumers, UK VAT at the 20% standard rate arises under the UK VAT (Place of Supply of Services) Rules 1992 and Part 1 of Schedule 3A Value Added Tax Act 1994, because Gibraltar is treated as a non-UK territory for VAT; compliance is through the HMRC VAT Non-Union Mini One Stop Shop portal for digital services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A – No indirect-tax registration threshold applies in Gibraltar or Bermuda because no VAT/GST regime exists; no turnover trigger for consumption tax registration is prescribed by law. For UK VAT, a mandatory registration threshold of £85,000 (GBP) of UK taxable supplies of digital services in a rolling 12-month period applies, and a simplified VAT on cross-border e-services registration may be used for supplies below that limit.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, digital stamping, or e-invoicing validation mandate for B2B or B2C SaaS invoices; commercial invoices suffice, preserved for six years. Bermuda likewise has no e-invoicing clearance system. If the Gibraltar entity elects voluntary UK VAT registration to serve UK B2C customers, it must file quarterly Making Tax Digital (MTD) VAT returns through HMRC-compatible software using a functional compatible bridging API to https://www.tax.service.gov.uk, but it does not require HMRC pre-clearance stamping of individual e-invoices, and only standard MTD digital record-keeping applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: No export zero-rating claim is available or necessary because Gibraltar and Bermuda do not impose VAT/GST on exports; the pure SaaS cloud subscription to overseas customers is outside the scope of any Gibraltar indirect tax and generates no negative VAT or refund right. For UK VAT purposes, where the SaaS is supplied from Gibraltar to non-UK overseas customers, the supply is 'outside the scope' rather than zero-rated and no refund of input tax is attributable. Physical IoT hardware/devices occasionally deployed with the PropTech platform (sensors, gateways) are exported under the UK-Gibraltar Customs Trade Partnership and may be exported free of export charges provided they are not in free circulation in the UK; documentary proof of export is required only for customs-duty purposes and does not create any VAT refund mechanism in Gibraltar.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: UK-Gibraltar Customs Trade Partnership electronic Export Declaration (Exports System via Customs Declaration Service CDS) – required only where tangible IoT hardware is physically exported from Gibraltar

Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing movement of any tangible goods; for pure SaaS, a software delivery certificate (activation log and server access record, issued through API) replaces the transport document as the export substantiator

Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/MT950 bank statement from the Gibraltar-licensed bank or UK EMI evidencing receipt of export consideration in hard currency within the 180-day repatriation benchmark
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Although Gibraltar lacks a zero-rating refund mechanism to be falsely claimed, mis-invoicing foreign customers to avoid UK VAT where the supply is UK-consumed triggers HMRC penalties under VATA 1994 Schedule 24 of up to 100% of evaded VAT plus interest, extending to criminal conviction for cheating the public revenue. Gibraltar Income Tax Office audit powers permit assessments within six years, and up to twenty-one years on the basis of fraud or deliberate neglect; civil penalties of up to 100% of the undercharged tax, plus fines up to £10,000 for non-production of documents, are statutorily available. Customs misdeclarations of tangible exports attract forfeiture of the goods, an amount equal to the unpaid customs duty, a civil penalty of up to 100% of duty, and retrospective withdrawal of export facilitation within four years; fraudulent export claims constitute a customs crime triable before the Supreme Court of Gibraltar with imprisonment of up to seven years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary anchor for Stering area; Gibraltar Pound issued by the Government of Gibraltar at 1:1 GBP peg); Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as the statutory prudential and AML/CFT supervisor for licensed banks, EMIs, and payment institutions; Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) as the exchange-control authority for the Bermuda Exempted Company; HMRC/FCA rules apply to any UK-resident payment corridors.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: UK and Gibraltar maintain unrestricted current- and capital-account convertibility with no exchange control legislation. GIP is freely convertible only via licensed banks at the fixed Sterling parity. Bermuda operates the Exchange Control Act 1972; the Exempted Company must obtain and maintain BMA 'Non-Resident' designation to be treated outside the exchange-control net, eliminating prior-permission requirements for inbound equity, intercompany loans, and profit repatriation. No Gibraltar withholding tax applies to dividends or interest remitted to the Bermuda parent, and the Bermuda exempt company benefits from full tax-exempt status. SaaS subscription receivables may be retained in any currency without conversion obligation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender, conversion ratio, or statutory retention timeline applies to export receipts or SaaS revenue in Gibraltar or the United Kingdom. For Bermuda, the Exchange Control Regulations historically require resident entities to offer foreign-currency export proceeds to an authorized dealer within six months of receipt; however, a BMA-designated non-resident Exempted Company is wholly exempt from such offer-for-sale and conversion duties. The PropTech platform may retain and net USD, GBP, and EUR treasury balances freely.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Operational Account (GBP/USD/EUR); segregated Capital Escrow sub-account
Operational Account and merchant-settlement clearing account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Santander Totta S.A. - Gibraltar Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; trade and LC enabling lines
Capital Escrow custody account and private-banking treasury
Corporate Operational Account (wealth-oriented lending and FX)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-high feasibility. FCA-authorized UK EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Currencycloud, Tide) will onboard a Bermuda Exempted Company remotely through video KYC and a certified corporate package; legal constraints are that post-Brexit passporting into Gibraltar requires recognition by the GFSC under the Financial Services (Transitional) regime or a Gibraltar e-money license, and EMIs cannot lawfully operate custodial escrow for rental-screening funds unless their permission expressly covers safeguarding and payment-account services. Consumer-grade EMIs must not be used to hold landlord float.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Bermuda Exempted Company directors are not legally required to appear physically; however, a Gibraltar-licensed corporate service provider (CSP) or registered agent must attend a face-to-face interview at the bank premises presenting original directors passports, an apostilled Register of Directors, and the BMA non-resident certificate. GIB and Trusted Novus Bank accept fully remote video onboarding where the CSP already holds a bank relationship; Santander Totta and EFG mandate final in-person sign-off for offshore entities. UK EMIs uniformly permit 100% remote opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore Bermudian tax-exempt entity without Gibraltar substance; nominee director layers; UBO resident in mixed-tax jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing; BMA non-resident designation letter; certified Register of Directors and Members; UBO/organizational chart tracing to natural persons; apostilled Memorandum and Articles; Gibraltar CSP introducer letter; three years audited financials or opening capital statement; bank reference from Bermuda account; signed source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value micro-transactions from rental-screening card payments (Stripe billing and ACH) creating uncharacteristic velocity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed SaaS merchant-of-record agreement with Stripe; PCI DSS Level 1 attestation; transactional velocity model and historical projection; automated renter/landlord AML and adverse-media screening via World-Check or ComplyAdvantage; segregated safeguarding account for tenant pre-payments; Group AML policy and GFSC/FCA compliance sign-off.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Real-estate sector adjacency causing PEP, sanctions, and rental-fraud false positives.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Narrow line-of-business disclosure memo (ISIC 6201 platform only, no brokerage or property-sale escrow); negative-media and sanctions screening of all landlord clients against OFAC, UK, and Gibraltar lists; PEP declarations; jurisdiction blacklist policy; explicit contractual prohibition of cash and third-party payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguous equity or intercompany debt flowing from Bermuda into Gibraltar (thin capitalization or deemed distribution risk).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved group funding memorandum; executed arm-length intercompany loan agreement with market interest; CbCR and transfer-pricing documentation; FATCA/CRS classification certificate (NFFE-E); Gibraltar substance and tax-residence analysis evidencing board meetings in Gibraltar; stamped share register and Companies Act filing confirmation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route: Bermuda Exempted Company (BMA non-resident designated account) to Gibraltar licensed operational account, with onward sweeps to UK EMI and Faster Payments rails. Protocol: SWIFT MT103 carrying purpose code 'EQUI' (equity) or 'LOAN' (intercompany debt) in tag 70; tag 72 to include UBO name and KYC reference; attach BMA exchange-control permission letter where capital exceeds USD 1,000,000; no Gibraltar or UK approval required for inward remittance. Preclear large GBP/USD/EUR conversions with the bank FX desk 48 hours in advance; ensure beneficiary bank account legal name exactly matches records to prevent sanctions false positives.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA/UK suppliers and intercompany settlements; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for EU/EEA software and cloud-infrastructure vendors; (iii) UK Faster Payments (up to GBP 1m per transaction) and CHAPS same-day clearing for high-value UK disbursements; (iv) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600, SWIFT MT700) for hardware procurement or data-center leases above USD 250,000; (v) Stripe/Bill.com API-initiated ACH for US landlord and property-manager disbursements. No surrender, license, or conversion restrictions apply to any outbound remittance from Gibraltar or the UK.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts with T+2 settlement (GBP/USD/EUR crosses)
Outright FX forwards up to 24 months tenor under ISDA/CSA with licensed Gibraltar, UK, and EU banks
FX vanilla options and zero-premium collars
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for intercompany loan and treasury rebalancing above GBP 5 million
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for illiquid emerging-market operational currencies in landlord-tenant vendor corridors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Bermuda Exempted Company (overseas company registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of the Gibraltar overseas company registration date (the annual return date); using the last day of the incorporation month as reference.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GIP 60 (USD 78) for up to 3 months, GIP 120 (USD 156) beyond 3 months; after 12 consecutive months of non-filing, the Registrar may issue a notice of intention to strike off the company; prosecution may result in a fine of up to GIP 5,000 (USD 6,500).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation Statement (UBO filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies House Gibraltar / Registrar of Beneficial Ownership (BOSS system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than the statutory annual return deadline, and within 14 days of any relevant change to the beneficial ownership or register of members.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to GIP 5,000 (USD 6,500) and daily default fine of GIP 100 (USD 130); material false statements attract imprisonment up to 6 months; no automatic strike-off but repeated default can trigger a Registrar's inquiry and court-ordered compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Accounts filing (transparent or available for public record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the financial year end; if the company is small or micro-entity, unaudited abbreviated accounts may be filed; an overseas company must file a copy of its audited parent accounts if applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil penalty of GIP 150 (USD 195) for filings up to 1 month late, escalating to GIP 1,000 (USD 1,300) after 6 months; the Registrar may also refuse to accept late accounts, and persistent default leads to a strike-off petition.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office (for economic substance compliance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 12 months after the accounting period end; the initial economic substance notification is due within 30 days of commencing operations or registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of GIP 300 (USD 390) per day following the notice period for failing to file, up to a maximum of GIP 10,000 (USD 13,000); failure to satisfy economic substance tests can result in the imposition of a penalty equal to the relevant tax loss and possible strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit is mandatory if the company does not qualify as small. For Gibraltar companies, the small-company exemption applies when two or more of the following are not exceeded: annual turnover of GIP 10.2 million (USD 13.3 million); balance sheet total of GIP 5.1 million (USD 6.6 million); average of 50 employees. The company in scope (ISIC 6201 PropTech SaaS) will require an audited balance sheet if it exceeds these thresholds or if an interest in it is given to the public.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 requires accounts to be prepared under UK-adopted International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or Financial Reporting Standard 102 (FRS 102); micro-entities may use FRS 105 'The Financial Reporting Standard applicable to the Micro-entities Regime'. The Bermuda Exempted Company's consolidated group statements may follow Bermuda GAAP if considered capable of equivalent presentation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017, the Bermuda Exempted Company, as a registered overseas company in Gibraltar, must maintain a register of beneficial owners at its Gibraltar registered office. An annual confirmation statement must be delivered to the Registrar of Companies on or before the annual return date, confirming the accuracy of the register. The register must record every individual holding more than 25% of shares or voting rights, and any transfer of shares must be reflected in the register within 14 days. The confirmation filing is separate from the annual return and is subject to its own non-compliance penalties.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (Bermuda Exempted Company statutory rate); 12.5% Gibraltar territorial corporate tax rate applies only if the company is Gibraltar-resident or earns Gibraltar-source trading profit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective on non-Gibraltar-source and non-UK-source income; no Bermuda corporation tax on exempted company profits; no capital gains tax; no UK corporation tax on non-UK income for non-UK resident shareholders; possible Gibraltar IP box and investment incentives for qualifying intellectual property income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Companies Tax Return (Form GTC-1); filed via Gibraltar Income Tax Office electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File no later than 12 months after the end of the accounting period; nil returns for exempt companies must still be filed if Gibraltar-source income is absent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Company Name and Tax Reference
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, Gibraltar registered office, unique tax reference and tax residence declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the entity as a Bermuda Exempted Company with central management and control exercised outside Gibraltar; attach tax residence certificate or board minute.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Period start date, period end date and reporting currency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use GBP for Gibraltar purposes; translate Bermuda or USD statutory accounts consistently using the annual average exchange rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declared Gibraltar-source trading income, deductible expenses, capital allowances, losses and assessable profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only profits arising in Gibraltar; foreign PropTech subscription income should be included in the tax reconciliation memorandum but excluded from assessable profits if the company is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of tax at 12.5%, foreign tax credits, withholdings and net tax due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave nil where no Gibraltar-source income is present; attach an officer certificate confirming that the Bermuda Exempted Company has not conducted Gibraltar-source trade.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Initial late filing penalty of GBP 100; daily surcharge of GBP 10 per day up to 90 days; extended failure penalty of GBP 100 and additional tax-geared penalty of up to 10% of unpaid tax; interest applies at 8% per annum on any late-paid tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Return (Form EC/AF-1) filed through Bermuda Registrar of Companies eCompanies portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the anniversary of incorporation or as stated in the annual compliance notice; annual government fee must be paid before the due date to avoid automatic strike-off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certificate number issued by the Bermuda Registrar of Companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the registered agent in Bermuda inserts the exact certificate number and confirms the entity is a non-resident Exempted Company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Registered Office and Resident Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bermuda registered office address and licensed resident agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Bermuda resident agent must be appointed; the company cannot register an office outside Bermuda without the agent confirming the statutory position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ultimate beneficial owner, directors and PSC details for the exempted company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the economic and ownership declaration; if the ultimate UK owner exercises management control from the UK, disclose that fact and consider UK tax residence consequences.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual fee triggers automatic dissolution; reinstatement costs and daily penalties apply; directors may be personally liable for continued trading after striking-off and may face disqualification.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0%; Gibraltar does not levy dividend withholding tax and Bermuda imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid by an Exempted Company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because the statutory dividend withholding rate is nil, no treaty relief is necessary for outbound dividends. If inbound dividends from a treaty jurisdiction suffer foreign tax, file Form DTA/TR-104 with the Gibraltar Income Tax Office, attach the foreign tax certificate, submit a Gibraltar tax residence certificate and a Bermuda certificate of residence, and claim foreign tax credit or treaty reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate is 0% in Gibraltar and Bermuda for royalties and interest; typical DTA rates are also 0%; SaaS subscription, rental-screening software licensing and intra-group interest can be repatriated gross without withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GBP 10,000,000 group turnover for Master File; GBP 1,000,000 aggregated related-party transactions for Local File; all controlled transactions are subject to the arm's length principle regardless of threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Gibraltar's Economic Substance Regulations and Bermuda's Economic Substance Act 2018 require adequate substance for entities conducting relevant activities. A PropTech real estate SaaS platform deriving IP royalties or financing income in a no-tax environment must demonstrate local decision-making, qualified staff, and physical presence. Pure equity holding and low-tier IP holding are subject to reduced substance requirements, but a sham or letterbox arrangement cannot rely on the 0% rate and will be recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Gibraltar-source SaaS revenue from Form GTC-1; falsifying PropTech subscription records; concealing the UK-resident beneficial owner while claiming pure non-residence; or using the Bermuda Exempted Company to receive taxable rental-screening fees without filing appropriate returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlimited fine and imprisonment up to 7 years for tax evasion; tax-geared penalty up to 200% of evaded tax; daily default fines of GBP 300; asset freezing and confiscation orders under the Proceeds of Crime Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate are personally liable for evaded tax and penalties; the corporate veil will be pierced; travel bans and passport seizure may be imposed; civil restitution orders require repayment of hidden profits; director disqualification up to 15 years and custodial sentence are available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a mailbox office, appointing nominee directors, holding no board meetings, and keeping no commercial records while claiming central management and control outside the UK; invoicing PropTech service fees from the exempted company solely to avoid UK corporation tax and VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation as UK tax resident under CTA 2009 s.14 and UK corporation tax at 19%; CFC charge and GAAR counteraction; Gibraltar registry strike-off for non-compliance; criminal fine up to GBP 5,000 for failure to maintain accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes where the company is a sham; liability for fraudulent trading under the Companies Act; civil recovery from directors' personal assets; disqualification and imprisonment up to 10 years for continuing to trade abusively after strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive management fees, paying royalties for software barely developed outside the group, or routing tenant-screening subscription profits through Bermuda without appropriate arm's length benchmarking; failing to prepare Master File and Local File despite exceeding the GBP 1,000,000 related-party threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Profits adjusted to arm's length; additional tax and interest at 8%; penalty up to 100% of the additional tax; documentation penalties up to GBP 30,000; UK HMRC may allocate profits under Part 4 TIOPA and impose a penalty up to 100% for careless or deliberate transfer pricing error.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs false transfer pricing declarations faces a personal tax-geared penalty and liability for 50% of the underpaid tax; financing deductions may be denied; director disqualification and criminal prosecution for knowingly misleading tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / CDD Breach and Unauthorised Payment Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing landlord and tenant payments on the PropTech platform without conducting AML/KYC checks; allowing rental deposits to be converted into crypto-asset payouts; acting as an unlicensed money service business using the Bermuda Exempted Company to conceal the payment flow; failing to report suspicious activity to the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlimited financial penalties under the Gibraltar Proceeds of Crime Act and AML Regulations 2019; GFSC penalty up to GBP 2 million or 10% of turnover; criminal money laundering conviction with imprisonment up to 14 years; freezing orders and confiscation of assets; EU/UK payment services regulatory fines if unauthorized activities fall within FSMA 2000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the AML/MLRO Officer are personally liable for failure to file suspicious activity reports; civil restitution of misappropriated client funds; travel bans during investigation; director disqualification and theft or fraud charges where deposits are diverted for personal benefit.
